tasks.short: Work with investment bankers to identify prospects, prepare pitches and build corporate client relationships.

steps.what: Review prospect records, past contacts and available financial information.
Agree target clients, relationship owners and the reason to approach each prospect.
Prepare a prospect brief and talking points for the planned approach.

loop.input: Approved approach plan, source documents and permitted contact history.
loop.output: Draft prospect brief and talking points with source references.
loop.check: Check names and figures against sources; analyst reviews relevance and confidential content.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass; unsupported claims become gaps for manual completion.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates populate facts, but connecting a prospect's circumstances to an approach needs free-text synthesis.

steps.what: Arrange the client meeting and circulate its agenda.
Discuss the client's priorities and explain how the team could help.
Record agreed next actions and assign follow-up owners.

loop.input: Analyst-written meeting notes and existing relationship owner records.
loop.output: Proposed activity record and follow-up actions.
loop.check: Each action cites a note passage; analyst verifies owners, dates and commitments before saving.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction pass; ambiguous commitments remain unassigned for manual entry.
loop.why_not_simpler: Meeting notes express commitments in varied language; fixed fields alone cannot reliably interpret them.

tasks.design: Configure prospect views in the {CRM} and use a bounded drafting loop to prepare source-linked briefs in the {DOCS}. The {CALENDAR} handles scheduling, while a reviewed extraction writes agreed follow-up actions into the {CRM}; bankers approve external invitations and conduct client conversations.
tasks.previous_blocker: Contact history and financial documents were scattered. Relevant pitch preparation required reading, while relationship choices resisted fixed rules.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing views and scheduling features handle routine coordination. AI-assisted coding makes document retrieval and small, checked drafting loops cheaper to assemble.
tasks.still_hard: Winning access, interpreting unstated priorities and protecting relationship-sensitive information remain difficult. Contact records may be incomplete.
tasks.human_edge: Build trust, choose a credible approach and recognise when the client needs a different conversation.

ambition.what: A fortnightly prospect-focus decision using current relationship and financial signals.

tasks.altitude: The analyst spends less time assembling briefs and more time discussing client fit with bankers. They can recommend prospect priorities more often; approval and client-commitment rights do not change.

reach.task: Assess whether a proposed client mandate fits capacity and commercial priorities.
reach.learn: Mandate economics, relationship conflicts and capacity planning.

reach.task: Maintain a useful prospect pipeline view.
reach.learn: Contact deduplication, pipeline definitions and access-controlled reporting.

evidence.claim: Prospect views, scheduling and structured follow-up records can largely use existing configuration.
Moody's Credit Memo drafts financial narratives from financial spreads and deal documents; this supports document drafting, not relationship automation.
GDPR applies to personal contact data; national rules determine whether employee consultation is required.

assumptions: This task describes a corporate-finance advisory team within a mid-size firm; many ordinary companies have no client-attraction mandate.
The team already maintains prospect records in the {CRM}.
Preparation uses permitted documents and written meeting notes rather than recording conversations.
Time shares are modelling estimates; the relationship-heavy prior is retained.
Build ranges cover one team and exclude procurement of new licensed financial data.
unknowns: Available {CRM} features, interfaces and contact-data quality.
Which financial sources the firm may reuse in client materials.
Who approves outreach and external commitments.
Applicable national consultation requirements and existing employee agreements.
research_questions: Which preparation fields are already available through configured {CRM} views?
Can sampled briefs achieve useful relevance without unsupported claims?
Which follow-up fields can be extracted reliably from existing written notes?
new_work: Review draft briefs and extracted commitments.
Resolve duplicate contacts and missing relationship history.
Maintain brief templates, access filters and extraction checks.

tasks.short: Assess the financial returns and risks of green construction and retrofit investments.

steps.what: Read engineering reports and supplier quotes into project cost and savings inputs.

loop.input: Engineering reports and supplier quotes for the specified project.
loop.output: Draft cost, savings, timing and warranty fields with source locations.
loop.check: Validate currency, units, quote totals and dates; analyst accepts each material input.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction pass per document; missing or conflicting fields go to manual review.
loop.why_not_simpler: Reports and quotes vary in layout and express exclusions and savings assumptions in free text.

steps.what: Export actual costs, energy consumption and tariffs into the analysis workbook.
Set defensible assumptions for savings, useful life, funding and project risks.
Calculate project cash flows, net present value, payback and financing effects.
Run sensitivities for energy prices, savings shortfalls, delays and cost overruns.
Write the investment recommendation, explaining uncertainties and conditions for proceeding.

loop.input: Validated valuation, sensitivity results, assumptions and analyst-selected recommendation.
loop.output: Draft investment recommendation with conditions and source-linked figures.
loop.check: Insert figures deterministically; analyst checks uncertainty wording and that conclusions reflect their recommendation.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass; unresolved claims remain flagged for manual writing.
loop.why_not_simpler: Tables can be templated, but explaining project-specific uncertainties requires contextual prose.

steps.what: Challenge the recommendation and approve, defer or reject the proposed investment.

tasks.design: Integrate baseline data from the {ERP} and {OPS_SYSTEM} into the {DATA_PLATFORM}, using a bounded extraction loop for documents in the {DOCS}. Deterministic calculations produce valuations and sensitivity views in the {BI}, then a bounded loop drafts the recommendation; people approve material inputs, assumptions and investment decisions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Baseline data needed manual reconciliation, and each project workbook repeated financial logic. Engineering assumptions still required specialist judgement.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding reduces the effort of building reusable calculations and source adapters. Checked document extraction can reduce rekeying without changing who accepts the assumptions.
tasks.still_hard: Realised savings depend on engineering performance, occupancy, weather and delivery. Subsidy eligibility, baseline adjustments and uncertain future tariffs remain costly to establish.
tasks.human_edge: Challenge optimistic savings, identify omitted costs and weigh uncertain financial returns against operational objectives.

ambition.what: A lightweight retrofit investment assessment for smaller company sites.

tasks.altitude: The analyst spends more time testing engineering assumptions and comparing competing projects. They can offer smaller sites a structured assessment; investment approval rights do not change.

reach.task: Check retrofit cost estimates and scope exclusions.
reach.learn: Estimate classes, contingency treatment and construction scope boundaries.

reach.task: Place approved retrofit investments in the capital budget.
reach.learn: Capital prioritisation, phasing and budget constraints.

evidence.claim: Cash-flow valuation and sensitivity calculations can use deterministic code once inputs and assumptions are defined.
DataSnipper supports source-linked financial evidence checks with team review; this is adjacent evidence for input verification.
The digest reports an incorrect cash waterfall in an Excel-agent test, supporting independent arithmetic checks rather than model-calculated valuations.
GDPR applies where project data contain personal information; employee consultation depends on national rules and the proposed use.

assumptions: Energy consumption is available through the {OPS_SYSTEM} or a governed export.
The first build covers one project category and an agreed valuation method.
The analysis concerns company assets rather than individual consumer credit decisions.
Financial arithmetic is highly automatable; engineering and investment judgement remain substantial despite the automation prior.
Build ranges exclude creating missing meters, commissioning engineering studies or obtaining subsidy rulings.
unknowns: Availability and granularity of energy and cost data.
Approved discount rates, tax treatment and investment thresholds.
Who validates savings estimates and baseline adjustments.
Applicable subsidy conditions and national consultation requirements.
research_questions: Which baseline adjustments materially change project rankings?
Can the reusable calculation reproduce accepted workbooks and known edge cases?
Which quote fields require specialist review rather than extraction alone?
new_work: Review extracted exclusions, costs and savings inputs.
Resolve missing consumption periods and incompatible units.
Maintain valuation rules, tariff feeds and project templates.
Compare realised savings with approved assumptions.

tasks.short: Discuss corporate debt options with clients and agree a suitable refinancing or restructuring approach.

steps.what: Read debt agreements and financial statements to assemble the client's current debt position.

loop.input: Debt agreements, financial statements and the client-provided cash forecast.
loop.output: Draft debt position with balances, maturities, security and covenant references.
loop.check: Tie balances to statements; reviewer checks material clauses, amendments and source locations.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction pass; conflicting terms or missing amendments require manual examination.
loop.why_not_simpler: Debt terms and amendments use varied contractual language that fixed parsers cannot fully capture.

steps.what: Calculate repayment schedules, funding gaps and illustrative refinancing scenarios.
Discuss priorities, constraints, lender relationships and acceptable trade-offs with the client.
Select a recommended approach using updated scenarios and the client's stated constraints.
Write the advice summary, conditions and next actions.

loop.input: Analyst-selected debt recommendation, checked scenarios and written meeting notes.
loop.output: Draft advice summary with conditions, uncertainties and next actions.
loop.check: Figures come from checked calculations; analyst verifies that advice and commitments match their recommendation.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass; unsupported terms or commitments require manual writing.
loop.why_not_simpler: Explaining client-specific trade-offs and conditional advice needs contextual prose beyond a fixed template.

steps.what: Review the advice and approve its release to the client.
Send the approved advice and confirm next actions with the client.

tasks.design: Use a bounded loop to extract debt terms from the {DOCS}, then run checked repayment and covenant calculations on the {DATA_PLATFORM}. A second bounded loop drafts the analyst's selected advice in the {DOCS}, while the {WORKFLOW} routes release approval and prepares the {EMAIL}; client discussions and substantive recommendations remain with advisers.
tasks.previous_blocker: Contracts and amendments needed reading, while scenario work relied on separate workbooks. Client constraints and lender dynamics could not be reduced to repayment arithmetic.
tasks.enabler_now: Reusable calculations and inexpensive document adapters reduce preparation work. Bounded extraction and drafting can assist advisers when every material term remains traceable.
tasks.still_hard: Distressed situations, uncertain lender appetite and legal interpretations remain demanding. Better calculations do not establish that refinancing is available or suitable.
tasks.human_edge: Understand the client's tolerance for risk, negotiate difficult trade-offs and recognise when legal or restructuring specialists are needed.

ambition.what: A quarterly corporate debt-maturity and covenant-headroom review.

tasks.altitude: The analyst spends less time reconstructing debt schedules and more time testing options with clients. They can provide earlier warnings through a recurring review; advice-release and transaction authority do not change.

reach.task: Maintain a forward view of liquidity and refinancing needs.
reach.learn: Liquidity buffers, funding calendars and lender reporting.
Stress scenarios, floating-rate exposure and covenant interpretation.

evidence.claim: Repayment schedules and numerical covenant tests can be deterministic when contractual terms are validated.
Moody's Credit Memo drafts financial memos from spreads and deal documents; this supports drafting assistance, not autonomous debt advice.
Natural-person creditworthiness scoring can fall within the EU AI Act's high-risk categories; that is a separate scope from the assumed corporate advisory workflow.
GDPR applies to personal information in client records; advisory obligations and employee consultation depend on national rules.

assumptions: Clients are corporate legal entities; consumer and sole-trader lending require a separate legal and workflow assessment.
The task covers advice and discussion, not signing financing agreements or moving funds.
Client records include the relevant debt amendments.
Conversation and judgement retain most of the work; preparation and paperwork offer narrower gains.
Build ranges cover an agreed family of debt instruments rather than every possible covenant structure.
unknowns: Actual client types and regulated advisory activities.
Completeness of debt agreements, amendments and cash forecasts.
Advice-release authority and professional review requirements.
Permitted document processing, retention and applicable national consultation requirements.
research_questions: Which contractual clauses can be represented safely as explicit calculation rules?
How often do missing amendments change the apparent debt position?
Which financing scenarios are genuinely actionable given lender appetite?
new_work: Review extracted terms and resolve contractual ambiguity.
Check draft advice for unsupported commitments.
Refresh forecasts and record reasons for departures from standard scenarios.

tasks.short: Prepare and present client materials explaining financial plans, options, risks and next decisions.

steps.what: Collect the approved recommendation, supporting calculations and relevant client requirements.
Choose the presentation's sequence, emphasis and decisions to put before the client.
Build charts and tables from the checked financial calculations.
Write concise explanations of the plan, alternatives, risks and proposed next actions.

loop.input: Approved recommendation, analyst-selected outline and checked chart data.
loop.output: Draft slide explanations and speaker notes with source references.
loop.check: Insert figures deterministically; analyst checks fidelity, qualifications and suitability for the intended audience.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass; missing evidence or unclear advice requires manual completion.
loop.why_not_simpler: Fixed text cannot adequately explain client-specific alternatives and trade-offs in concise language.

steps.what: Assemble the deck, apply the template and adjust slide layout.
Review figures, disclosures and message clarity, then approve the deck for client use.
Present the plan, answer questions and record the client's requested changes or decision.

tasks.design: A deterministic generator on the {DATA_PLATFORM} assembles source packs, charts and template-based decks from approved material in the {DOCS} and checked financial data. A bounded loop drafts explanations, automated checks flag numerical and layout errors, and a senior adviser approves the presentation before the analyst uses it with the client.
tasks.previous_blocker: Copying charts, matching versions and adjusting layouts consumed time. Generic templates did not explain client-specific financial choices.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding lowers the cost of building a reusable deck generator and rendering checks. A bounded drafting loop can work from approved advice rather than inventing a plan.
tasks.still_hard: Persuasive sequencing, suitable disclosures and unusual layouts still need judgement. Explaining uncertainty and answering unexpected questions remain human work.
tasks.human_edge: Choose what the client needs to understand, explain uncomfortable trade-offs and adapt to questions in the room.

ambition.what: A one-page funding-options explainer for client operational leaders.

tasks.altitude: The analyst spends less time formatting and more time rehearsing explanations and checking client understanding. They can provide a concise companion explainer; advice and approval rights do not change.

reach.task: Create financial charts that communicate options accurately.
reach.learn: Chart selection, uncertainty displays and accessible visual design.

reach.task: Review client-facing disclosures and permitted financial claims.
reach.learn: Disclosure standards, audience suitability and evidence retention.

evidence.claim: Charts, tables and template-based deck assembly can use deterministic generators.
Moody's Credit Memo demonstrates source-based financial narrative drafting; the digest does not establish a client-presentation case.
Baker Tilly Netherlands reported statement tick-and-tie falling from eight to two hours using DataSnipper; this vendor case supports verification assistance, not deck-generation savings.
GDPR applies to personal information in client materials; national rules govern any relevant employee consultation.

assumptions: This example presents a corporate funding plan, connecting it to the debt-advice workflow.
The recommendation and underlying calculations are approved before deck generation.
The first build supports a small set of stable presentation templates.
The task includes a short client presentation; deck production accounts for more time than the meeting prior suggests.
Build ranges exclude redesigning the firm's visual identity or producing bespoke layouts for every engagement.
unknowns: Supported presentation formats and template variability.
Required disclosures and client-release approval roles.
Available source interfaces, retention rules and national consultation requirements.
research_questions: Which recurring slides can be generated without bespoke layout work?
Can rendered decks reliably expose clipped text, missing labels and mismatched figures?
Do clients understand the generated explanations and uncertainties?
new_work: Review narrative drafts and client-facing qualifications.
Handle unusual layouts and rendering failures.
Maintain templates, disclosure text and source-version links.
Keep chart and arithmetic checks aligned with financial models.

role.altitude: The analyst's week shifts from rekeying, calculation repetition and formatting toward challenging assumptions, comparing options and advising people. More frequent analysis supports broader recommendations; investment, advice-release and transaction authority remain with the existing decision makers.
reach: Work with Cost Estimators to challenge retrofit scope and contingency.
Work with Treasurers and Controllers to anticipate funding gaps and debt maturities.
Work with Business Intelligence Analysts to make financial evidence usable.
Work with Compliance Officers to maintain sound client-facing explanations.
skills_to_grow: Financial model validation and independent reconciliation.
Data provenance, access control and source licensing.
Clear client explanations and difficult financial conversations.
role.ambitious_version: Offer a recurring capital-and-funding review that combines smaller-site retrofit assessments with debt-maturity and covenant warnings, giving decision makers earlier, source-backed options.
